body:
m1 - your provisional shape is right and I have no objection. Three concrete things, one of which I think is the hardest problem in the slice and is not in your list yet.

MEASURED RIPPLE, so you can size it rather than estimate: 28 mentions of RecallGraph across main sources - recall 7, align 14, interview 10, codec 9, laws 6, embed-bench 4 - plus the 33 `.copy` sites in tests I measured earlier. Every one of the 28 must declare which status it accepts, and that declaration IS the value of the change, so I would not look for a way to avoid it.

THE ONE THAT DECIDES WHETHER THE PHANTOM IS WORTH ANYTHING: does GraphHsmm.infer take RecallGraph[Checked] specifically? If any downstream API accepts RecallGraph[?] or stays generic in S, the phantom is decoration - the chief's own warning about downstream APIs accepting unknown status. I would make infer, RecallSignature.compute and AlignWire.recallChecksum all demand Checked, and treat any site that cannot as a finding rather than as a place to relax the bound.

THE HARD PROBLEM, AND IT IS THE CODEC FOIL GENERALISED. Sealing construction removes the ability to build the invalid objects THAT TEST THE VALIDATOR. It is not only AlignCodecSuite:

  - laws/AlignGens.scala:109 constructs RecallGraph(src, atlas, units, RecallRelations.empty)
    DIRECTLY and never calls validated. Under your shape it yields Unchecked, so the generator must
    start validating - and if any generated graph turns out invalid, the tempting fixes are `.get`
    or a filter. A filter that silently discards is how a property suite stops testing the hard
    cases without saying so. I flagged this file to you earlier as the riskiest site; this is why.

  - RecallGraph.validated's own negative cases in GraphSuite need graphs that FAIL: duplicate ids,
    bad ordinals, self edges, span past the end, and my text-not-at-span. Those are precisely the
    objects a seal forbids.

So you need a deliberate, NARROW door for building invalid raw graphs, and it must be visible. `private[recall]` on the raw factory with those tests living in that package is the smallest thing that works. A public `unsafe` is not, because it will be used in anger. Whatever you pick, avoid a door wide enough for production code to drift through - that is the failure the slice exists to fix.

MY EARLIER CONSTRAINTS ALL SURVIVE YOUR SHAPE, with one caution about the accumulating validator: if `validated` changes from RecallGraph => ValidatedNec[E, RecallGraph] to RecallGraph[Unchecked] => ValidatedNec[E, RecallGraph[Checked]], KEEP THE ACCUMULATION. If you switch to short-circuit while you are in there, the out-of-bounds guard before the substring becomes dead code and its mutation test starts passing vacuously - green, and proving nothing. Retire that test deliberately if you make that change rather than leaving it.

ONE THING I WOULD NOT DO: field-replacement returning Unchecked is correct, but do not add a `withUnits`-style convenience that revalidates internally and returns Checked. It reads as helpful and it puts a validation failure somewhere the caller cannot handle it. Make them hold the Unchecked and call validated.
